_comment: ngsolve poisson#3 (VTKOutput writes .vtu natively; exported cells are linear, so subdivision is how P2+ detail reaches the file). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604, unit_square maxh 0.3, H1 order 2. .Do() produces exactly one .vtu and no XDMF or .h5 companion, and the header declares UnstructuredGrid. NGSolve writes the arrays as raw appended binary with 4-byte length prefixes, so the fixture follows the XML offsets rather than reading element text -- reading the text gives an empty array and reading it with an 8-byte prefix gives garbage; both were hit here. At subdivision 0 the cell-type array is exactly [5], the linear triangle, and the cell count equals the 24 mesh elements. CORRECTION: at subdivision 2 the types are [5, 9] -- NGSolve also emits linear QUADS -- so every exported cell is linear, which is the load-bearing half, but 'all linear triangles' holds only at subdivision 0. Subdivision is what adds samples: 72 points/24 cells become 360/240, and 198 of the exported values are ones the subdivision-0 file did not contain. Mutation: exporting the subdivision-2 file at subdivision 0 makes the two identical and the fixture fails on subdivision_adds_sample_points.
